results.evidence: WTA says the top of the rock is reached after gaining 400 ft; Best Hikes BC puts the switchback series at about 100 m (328 ft) of gain after a gentle start. The Mountaineers' Artist Point page says part of the first half mile is blasted out of the cliff, and the Forest Service says the plateau is reached in less than a mile. Together these support approach/climbing_route/itinerary (~400 ft, ~0.4-0.5 mi) and contradict beta's 0.6-1 mi and 'near 5,700 ft' plateau (5,700+ is the summit high point at the west end).

results.evidence: The Mountaineers route page is still the only source that states a best window (April-May, before brush fills the gullies). The Mountain Project description reports an early-June ascent with thin snow and says more snow makes the route easier, but names no window; a Jim Brisbine report climbed the North Brother mid-July with plenty of snow; CascadeClimbers reports record traverses on 6/1/2014 and May 2018. A second source explicitly recommending April-May (or June) would settle it.

results.correct_value: No wilderness permit is required in The Brothers Wilderness (Olympic National Forest); only a Northwest Forest Pass / interagency pass to park. A park permit applies only to camps inside Olympic National Park.
results.evidence: The Olympic National Forest wilderness page states plainly that no permit is needed to visit Olympic National Forest wilderness areas (The Brothers Wilderness is one of them), only a recreation pass at some trailheads. The Brothers SummitPost page says the wilderness is Forest Service land and no backcountry permit is required, only a Forest Service recreation pass. The FS Brothers Wilderness page lists the regulations (fires above 3,500 ft, group of 12) with no permit, and WTA lists only a NW Forest Pass / interagency pass.
